pins.title: What to write after every hike
pins.pinTitle: Hiking journal printable: what to write after a hike, with a free sample log page
pins.description: After each hike, write down eight things: the date, the trail, distance in miles and km, total time, the weather, who you hiked with, the best moment and one thing you would change next time. Our Trail Journal has a free one-page sample log to print or copy into any notebook.

pins.title: Thanksgiving weekend hike?
pins.pinTitle: Winter hiking checklist for beginners: what to wear and bring on a cold holiday weekend hike
pins.description: Planning a walk after the big meal? Pick a short trail you know, start early and be back an hour before sunset. Wear layers (no cotton), a hat, gloves and spare dry socks. Deer seasons are open in many states, so wear blaze orange and check your state wildlife agency for dates. Our beginner checklist has the full list.

pins.title: Dark by 5 pm?
pins.sub: Keep a headlamp in your pack.
pins.pinTitle: Rechargeable headlamp for winter hikes: wide beam, motion sensor, USB-C, a gift under $20
pins.description: Short winter days catch hikers out. Our motion-sensor headlamp has a wide COB light strip that lights the trail edges, a small spot LED for signs and blazes, and a wave-to-switch sensor that works with gloves on. USB-C rechargeable, rain resistant (IPX4). A useful gift under $20. Gear ships in 6-13 business days.

pins.title: Dark walks with your dog?
pins.pinTitle: LED dog collar for dark winter walks: USB rechargeable light-up collar, XS to XXL
pins.description: Winter evenings come early. A USB rechargeable LED collar makes your dog easy to see on dark trailheads, streets and park paths, with 3 light modes and sizes from XS to XXL. A practical gift for dog owners. Gear ships in 6-13 business days.

pins.title: Icy steps on the trail?
pins.sub: Chains that slip over your boots.
pins.pinTitle: Chain ice cleats for winter hiking: stainless steel spikes that stretch over your boots
pins.description: Icy trailheads, frozen boardwalks and packed snow are where most winter slips happen. These stainless steel chain ice cleats stretch over the boots you already wear and roll up small for your pack. One size fits most boots, about US women's 4 to US men's 11. Made for icy paths and trails, not steep ice or glaciers. Gear ships in 6-13 business days.

pins.title: Your phone won't read your gloves?
pins.sub: Wear a thin liner under a mitt.
pins.pinTitle: Do touchscreen gloves work for winter hiking? The liner-under-mitt setup that works
pins.description: Touchscreen gloves work for quick taps in mild cold, but not when they are wet, thick or loose at the fingertip, and thin ones are rarely warm enough alone. Wear a thin touchscreen liner under a warm mitt, keep your phone in an inside pocket and download your map at the car. Read the full guide in our Trail Journal.

pins.title: Cold train platform mornings?
pins.sub: Warm merino socks for the commute.
pins.pinTitle: Warm merino wool socks for the winter commute: cushioned crew socks for cold platforms
pins.description: Waiting on a cold platform or walking to the office in slush? Cushioned crew socks with 80% merino wool keep feet warm without getting sweaty and stay fresh through a long day. For the commute, home, travel and the trail. Two sizes, four colors.

pins.title: Early dog walks, warm feet
pins.pinTitle: Merino wool socks for winter dog walks: warm, soft cushioned crew socks for cold mornings
pins.description: Frosty sidewalks before work, snowy park loops after dark. Soft 80% merino wool crew socks with a cushioned sole keep your feet warm in boots on every winter dog walk, and they feel soft, not itchy. Two sizes, four colors.

pins.title: If a hike goes wrong
pins.pinTitle: Hiking emergency checklist printable: first aid kit list and what to do if things go wrong
pins.description: Build the kit once, check it before every trip, and know the steps before you need them. This printable hiking emergency checklist covers the emergency kit for your pack, a two-minute check before each hike, what to do if you get lost or someone is hurt, storms, cold and darkness, plus an emergency info card. Instant PDF download.

pins.title: New to hiking this winter?
pins.pinTitle: Beginner hiking guide printable: how to start hiking, first hike checklist and trail tips
pins.description: Thinking about starting to hike? This printable beginner hiking guide has twelve short chapters: choosing your first trail, what moderate really means, reading the weather, what to wear and pack, water and food, navigation, staying safe and trail etiquette, with a first hike checklist. Instant PDF download, print at home or read on your phone.
